rawFindings.title: Content changes can reuse the same cache-busting URL
rawFindings.explanation: The cache-busting query string is now derived from the file mtime instead of the file content. If a file's contents change while its mtime is preserved or unchanged at the filesystem timestamp resolution, Karma will generate the same script URL for different content, allowing the browser to reuse a cached stale file.
rawFindings.suggestion: Use a content-derived version again, such as `file.sha`, for generated script URLs and the served-file mappings, and keep computing it when files are processed/refreshed.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Serve `/base/app.js` with content `v1` and mtime `1700000000000`, then change its content to `v2` while restoring the same mtime. The generated context still references `/base/app.js?1700000000000`, so a browser with the previous response cached can run `v1` instead of `v2`.
